outcomes.text: Identify missing melody or rhythm sections from multiple-choice alternatives.
Name printed musical intervals.
Describe musical features in a short written response.
Identify, describe, or comment on musical features or aspects of their performance.
Recognise melodic movement, scalic and arpeggiated writing, countermelodies, phrases, improvisation, leitmotifs, range, fanfares, hooks, riffs, rāga and quarter-tones.
Identify major, minor, chromatic, modal, pentatonic, rāga and maqām scales or modes.
Recognise duple, triple, quadruple and irregular metres, simple and compound time, syncopation, hemiola, anacrusis, cross-rhythm, polyrhythm, habanera, marcado, clave and tāla.
Identify the key of a printed musical passage.
Identify major and minor tonality, modulation to related keys, and tonic major or minor.
Identify chords and cadences in recorded musical extracts.
Recognise primary and secondary chords, dominant and diminished sevenths, common cadences, consonant and dissonant harmony, diatonic and chromatic writing, suspensions and pedals.
Follow and interpret a printed score while listening.
Read staff notation using treble, bass and alto clefs; key signatures up to four sharps or flats; rhythms, rests, time signatures and common symbols.
Identify major, minor and perfect intervals, and transpose parts for specified trumpets, clarinets and horns to concert pitch.
Transpose short passages written for transposing instruments into concert pitch.
Identify the composer from several possible answers.
Identify ripieno, concertino, basso continuo, chamber ensembles, orchestral, keyboard, vocal, pop, rock, Latin American, Hindustani, silk-and-bamboo and takht instruments.
Recognise pizzicato, arco, glissando, portamento, pitch-bending, tremolo, double stopping, rolls, melisma, syllabic singing, rap, word-painting and word-setting.
Represent musical structure using suitable terms or letter patterns such as AABA.
Compare passages occurring within the same musical extract.
Comment on the musical context or style.
Identify binary, ternary, rondo, ritornello, episode, sonata form, introduction, cadenza, minuet and trio, theme and variations, strophic and through-composed forms.
Recognise intro, verse, chorus, bridge or middle eight, outro, breakdown, build-up, drop, call and response, and ālāp, jōr, gat and jhālā.
Recognise samples, loops, chorus, reverb, delay, overdubbing, double-tracking, multi-tracking and drum machines.
Recognise common Italian tempo markings, tempo changes including accelerando, rallentando and rubato, and beats per minute.
Identify monophonic, unison, octave doubling, homophonic, polyphonic, heterophonic, imitative, antiphonal, solo, tutti, cluster, drone and parallel textures.
Recognise repetition, ascending and descending sequences, imitation, ostinato, riff and Alberti bass.
Identify dynamic levels from pianissimo to fortissimo, crescendos, diminuendos and terraced dynamics.
Recognise legato, staccato, accents, sforzando, slurs, trills, mordents, turns, appoggiaturas and acciaccaturas.
Study Vivaldi’s Spring and selected movements from Handel’s Concerto Grosso in D to understand Baroque concertos, style and performance practice.
Listen to representative Baroque works by Corelli, Bach, Jacquet de la Guerre and Telemann, especially instrumental concerto and ensemble repertoire.
Study Mozart’s Piano and Winds Quintet to learn sonata form and characteristic features of Classical instrumental and chamber music.
Listen to representative Classical works by Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven, including chamber, variation, symphonic and concerto repertoire.
Study Smetana’s Vltava to understand Romantic orchestral writing, programme music and musical expressions of national identity.
Listen to representative Romantic works by Mendelssohn, Mayer, Borodin, Clara Schumann and Chopin.
Explore art songs, choral music, popular songs and musical-theatre songs from the twentieth century onward.
Understand how composers set words, using musical features to reinforce textual meaning and modern song structures and techniques.
Listen to examples by Libby Larsen, Jonathan Dove, Pasek and Paul, alongside suitable local, popular and musical-theatre repertoire.
Study tango, salsa and electronic dance music, recognising their characteristic instruments, musical features and cultural contexts.
Understand African and Western influences in Latin American dance music, and how technology and production techniques create EDM.
Listen to representative examples including Piazzolla’s Libertango, Lavoe’s El Cantante and F-777’s Viking Arena.
Study silk-and-bamboo ensembles, Hindustani classical music and Arab takht ensembles from varied cultural traditions.
Identify principal instruments, describe style-specific features and discuss the social and performance contexts of each tradition.
Listen to San Liu, rāga khamāj and Wasla en sabâ in the specified performances.
Study ballet, film and video-game music from the twentieth century onward, including orchestral music accompanying visual action.
Understand how musical features create atmosphere, heighten tension and excitement, and enhance particular dramatic or visual moments.
Listen to representative examples including The Rite of Spring, Star Wars and the Gran Saga soundtrack.
